ol.li: The sequence row is locked inside the same transaction as the ticket insert. Two IT staff encoding at the same second cannot receive the same number.
scope_key is the only thing that differs between date-scoped and year-scoped numbering — one config value, same locking, same code. This question is still open; see §3 of the design doc.

Backdating works for free under either scheme. Note the behavioural difference: date-scoped continues that date's run; year-scoped hands out the next global number, so a backdated ticket can carry a higher number than tickets on later dates.
The outbox row is written in the same transaction, so a ticket can never exist without a pending sync (and vice versa).
The queue job is dispatched after commit, so the worker never reads a row that hasn't landed yet.
